transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-16T16:00Z
Length: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Oliver Hayes (Head of Platform, Hearthstone), Priya Nair (Compliance), Evan Cole (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick residency/compliance discovery for inference hosting options — evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) for EU and multi-entity data; log retention and keystore residency are top blockers; next steps: SOC2/HIPAA artifacts, POC scheduling, benchmark run.

Topics: data residency, log retention, KMS/keystore, SSO/SAML, audit evidence, latency/cost tradeoffs, POC scope

Action items (captured): see metadata

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hi everyone, thanks for joining, um, we're excited to, to go through Hearthstone's needs around hosting and residency. quick intros?
[00:12] Oliver (Hearthstone): yeah hi, i'm oliver, i run platform. we're trying to understand whether we can run inference on redwood hosted, or we need dedicated or a private install given our european subsidiaries. compliance is the big driver.
[00:26] Priya (Hearthstone): priya here, compliance manager — HIPAA-ish for some clients, and GDPR obviously. we need clarity on audit logs and where keys live.
[00:35] Daniel (Redwood SE): thanks, daniel from redwood infra. i'll try to be concrete on latency/cost and how keystore/rotation works across regions.
[00:43] Evan (Hearthstone): evan cto — we'll be evaluating 2 workloads: a customer support summarization pipeline (low latency) and a batch-risk-scoring job (throughput).

[02:00] Maya: high level — three paths: 1) Redwood hosted (fastest), 2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), 3) Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem). each has different surface area for data flows and audit. do you have a hard requirement that no EU personal data leaves EU?
[02:18] Priya: yes. all personal data for our EU clients must remain in EU tenants, and we need proof — logs + keystore residency evidence. we also have to show separation between our us and eu tenants.
[02:33] Oliver: and for some clients, the requirement is stronger — keys need to be customer-managed KMS in-country.

[04:05] Daniel: right, for sponsored KMS we support a few patterns — customer-managed KMS in a cloud region (we integrate via KMS APIs), or HSM-backed on prem for private. note: sometimes our docs call it "keystore routing" but internal naming varies.
[04:28] Priya: do you support key escrow? like, we may require escrow for disaster recovery, but escrow must be in the same jurisdiction.
[04:38] Maya: yes there are enterprise options for escrow; we typically discuss with legal for SLA/escrow terms. i'll flag that with our compliance team.

[06:00] Evan: about logs — we need to limit raw transcript retention and produce redacted logs for audits. can you scope retention windows and who can access the logs?
[06:13] Daniel: we have per-customer retention configs. by default hosted keeps short-term raw logs for debugging then redacts. dedicated gives you more control over retention and access controls. private—full control. also we can stream sanitized audit logs to a customer S3 in-region.
[06:35] Oliver: streaming is interesting — do you support pushing logs to our Azure blob in eu-central?
[06:42] Daniel: yes, we support S3-compatible sinks, and have partners for Azure blob; sometimes the connectors are maintained as integrations. we'll include the connector doc.

[09:10] Priya: another concern: incidental PII in prompts. we need redaction or a policy to prevent retention of raw PII. do you provide automated PII scrubbers or is that a customer responsibility?
[09:23] Maya: we provide redaction tooling and configurable scrubbers as part of Optimize. that said, teams often augment with client-side filtering for the highest assurance.
[09:35] Priya: any guarantee for no PII entering US regions? e.g. if a request hits the US, even transiently, that's a compliance violation for some clients.
[09:46] Daniel: with Dedicated/EU pinning you can route all inference to EU-only pools. hosted by default routes regionally (but hosted multiregional falls back to nearest). we can set routing policy to hard-enforce EU region and disable US fallbacks for the POC.

[12:00] Oliver: what about model fallbacks? if a pinned model isn't available in EU, will the platform fallback to a different variant and potentially call an endpoint outside EU?
[12:12] Daniel: good question — by default we have fallback policies. for strict residency we can set policy to fail rather than fallback, or fallback to an EU-available quantized variant. we'll show the policy DSL in the follow-up.

[15:00] Priya: audit evidence: we need chain-of-custody for keys and proof that logs never left EU. what artifacts can you provide?
[15:12] Maya: we can provide access logs, cryptographic key metadata (thumbprints, rotation events), and signed attestations from our control plane for the dedicated offering. for private installs we provide customer-side logs. I'll attach a SOC2 + HIPAA mapping doc.

[18:30] Evan: latency for the support summarization is sensitive — target p95 < 400ms. can dedicated EU nodes hit that with our prompt sizes?
[18:42] Daniel: based on similar customers, dedicated with continuous batching and prefix caching should meet that — depending on model size and token distribution. we'll run a benchmark with your sample prompts. note: prefix caching and K V cache warm-up times matter — we'll capture cold vs warm p95.
[19:05] Oliver: okay, and cost delta between hosted and dedicated? we need rough per-1k token numbers to present to finance.
[19:16] Maya: i'll share a cost model doc. dedicated typically reduces unit cost at scale but requires commit. hosted is simpler for trials. we'll include a simple calc in the follow-up.

[22:00] Priya: SSO and user RBAC for model ops — we need SAML SSO and scoped roles for who can pull logs or get decrypted payloads.
[22:12] Daniel: yes, we support SAML, SCIM for provisioning, and role-based RBAC. we can show role mappings and how audit logs capture privilege escalation events.

[25:10] Oliver: any compliance gaps we should be aware of? e.g. things that would push us to private rather than dedicated?
[25:21] Maya: typical triggers for private: strict in-country keystore non-exportability, air-gapped requirements, or customer insistence on full network control. Dedicated covers most enterprise needs when combined with customer-managed KMS and in-region hosting.

[28:00] Priya: GDPR DSARs — we need an easy way to query and produce call transcripts per subject. can we run subject-level extractions from logs?
[28:14] Daniel: we can provide search/export tooling and a playbook for DSARs. note: if you opt for deep redaction, retrievability could be impacted — that's a policy choice.

[31:30] Evan: segmentation across subsidiaries — we have multiple EU legal entities; can we map each entity to distinct tenant controls and separate audit trails?
[31:42] Daniel: yes, multi-tenant segmentation is supported; we can have isolated tenants per legal entity with separate keystores and S3 sinks. gives you clean audit trails per entity.

[34:10] Priya: encryption at rest question — does Redwood encrypt model artifacts? who owns the encryption keys for model weights?
[34:21] Maya: model artifacts on dedicated/private are encrypted at rest using either our managed keys or customer-managed KMS keys depending on the contract. for hosted, we use provider-managed keys by default but customer-managed is an option for enterprise.

[37:50] Oliver: a logistic question — can you sign a data processing addendum (DPA) with subprocessor list? we need that for procurement.
[38:02] Maya: absolutely. we'll share our DPA and subprocessor list. procurement often asks for that before any POC.

[41:00] Daniel: small gotcha — our docs sometimes call the private offering "private control plane" which causes confusion. basically private gives you the control plane in your VPC and optionally air-gapped inference nodes.
[41:18] Priya: ok, good to clarify.

[44:00] Evan: for the POC scope: we want 2 things — (A) latency test for summarization in EU pinned nodes (p95 target) and (B) log retention + redaction proof for a sample of 10k interactions. can you run both?
[44:13] Daniel: yes, we can. we'll need sample data, a short auth token, and a list of endpoints to pin to EU. also need your KMS details if you want CMK in the POC.
[44:32] Oliver: timeline? we want results in ~2 weeks.
[44:37] Maya: we can aim for 2 weeks. i'll send initial artifacts today and propose POC dates.

[46:50] Priya: one more security thing — penetration testing and vulnerability disclosure policy. do you allow customer-validated pentests?
[46:59] Maya: yes, with a coordinated schedule and scoping. we'll share our VDP and the point of contact.

[49:00] Maya: recap — i'll send SOC2 + HIPAA mapping, DPA + subprocessors, and a regional hosting diagram. Daniel will run latency/cost benchmarks and the log-retention POC plan. Priya to share EU entity list and sample data attributes. schedule follow up POC kickoff for week of 2026-05-04.
[49:25] Oliver: thanks, that sounds good.
[49:32] Priya: thanks all.
[49:36] Evan: thanks.
[50:00] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and add materials into the CRM. bye.

References/Artifacts shared: SOC2 summary (link to sent doc placeholder), HIPAA control mapping spreadsheet (to be attached), regional-hosting-diagram.pdf (to be created), POC runbook (placeholder link).
